t:
(a) 
Section 202 (c) of the Housing and Rent Act of 1947, as amended, is amended by striking out paragraph (1) thereof and inserting in lieu thereof the following:


“(1) 

(A) those housing accommodations, in any establishment which is located in a city of Tess than two million five hundred thousand population according to the 1940 decennial census and which is commonly known as a hotel in the community in which it is located, which are occupied by persons who are provided customary hotel services  such as maid service, furnishing and laundering of linen, telephone and secretarial or desk service, use and upkeep of furniture and fixtures, and bellboy service; or


“(B) 
those housing accommodations in hotels in cities of two million five hundred thousand population or more according to the 1940 decennial census (i) which are located in hotels in which 75 per centum or more of the occupied housing accommodations on March 1, 1949, were used for transient occupancy, or (ii) which are not located in hotels described in (i) but which on March 1, 1949, were used for transient occupancy; for the purposes of this subparagraph (B)—

“(1) the term ‘used for transient occupancy’ means rented on a daily basis, to a tenant who had not on March 1, 1949, continuously resided in the hotel for ninety days or more; and
“(2) 
the term ‘hotel’ means any establishment which on June 30, 1947, was commonly known as a hotel in the community in which it is located and was occupied by an appreciable number of persons who were provided customary hotel services such as maid service, furnishing and laundering of linen, telephone and secretarial or desk service, use and upkeep of furniture and fixtures, and bellboy service; or”.






 
    (b) 
Section 202 (c) (2) of the Housing and Rent Act of 1947, as amended, is amended by striking out “trailer or trailer space” and inserting in lieu thereof “trailer, or trailer space, used exclusively for transient occupancy”.
 
    (c) 
Section 202 (c) of the Housing and Rent Act of 1947, as amended, is amended by striking out paragraph (3) thereof and inserting in lieu thereof the following:


“(3) 
any housing accommodations (A) the construction of which was completed on or after February 1, 1947, or which are housing accommodations created by a change from a nonhousing to a housing use on or after February 1, 1947, or which are additional housing accommodations created by conversion on or after February 1, 1947: Provided, however, That any housing accommodations resulting from any conversion created on or after the effective date of the Housing and Rent Act of 1949 shall continue to be controlled housing accommodations unless the Housing Expediter issues an order decontrolling them, which he shall issue if he finds that the conversion resulted in additional, self  contained family units as defined by regulations issued by him: And provided further, That contracts for the rental of housing accommodations to veterans of World War II and their immediate families, the construction of which was assisted by allocations or priorities under Public Law 388, Seventy-ninth Congress, approved May 22, 1946, shall remain in full force and effect; or (B) the construction of which was completed on or after February 1, 1945, and prior to February 1, 1947, and which between the date of completion and June 30, 1947, both dates inclusive, at no time were rented (other than to members of the immediate family of the landlord) as housing accommodations;or”.



 
    (d) 
Section 202 (d) of such Act, as amended, is amended by striking out “in which maximum rents were being regulated under such Act on March 1, 1947”, and inserting in lieu thereof the following: “in which maximum rents (1) were being regulated under such Act on March 1, 1947, or (2) are established or reestablished pursuant to section 204 (i) (1) or (2) of this title”.
 
    (e) 
Section 202 (e) of the Housing and Rent Act of 1947, as amended, is amended to read as follows:


“(e) 
The term ‘rent’ means the consideration, including any bonus, benefit, or gratuity demanded or received for or in connection with the use or occupancy of housing accommodations, or the transfer of a lease of housing accommodations.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this section only amends definitions of controlled housing accommodations and involves no outside-party process. However, it makes the Housing Expediter's decontrol orders turn on whether a conversion created self-contained family units "as defined by regulations issued by him," which contemplates the agency issuing regulations. Under the definition, authority or a requirement to make rules counts as participation, even when the reference is brief. The call is not certain because the rulemaking reference is incidental to the definitional amendments.
fable.s: contained family units as defined by regulations issued by him

qwen_block.w: This section amends the Housing and Rent Act of 1947 by redefining terms such as 'hotel,' 'transient occupancy,' and 'rent.' It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The reference to 'regulations issued by him' is a citation to existing regulatory authority for defining terms, not a mandate for a participatory process like a public comment period or advisory board. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_block.s: The term ‘rent’ means the consideration, including any bonus, benefit, or gratuity demanded or received for or in connection with the use or occupancy of housing accommodations, or the transfer of a lease of housing accommodations.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "regulations issued by him" (by the Housing Expediter) implies a rulemaking process that could involve public participation. However, the text itself does not mandate or describe any public comment period, hearing, or consultation; it merely references regulations as a mechanism for defining terms. Furthermore, the section is primarily about amending definitions of housing accommodations and rents, which are substantive legal definitions rather than procedural mandates for public input. The definition of participation requires that the government *consult or coordinate* with outsiders *before* making a decision. This section defines what constitutes controlled housing and rent, but does not establish a process for outsiders to participate in those definitions.

opus.w: The section makes the Housing Expediter's decontrol decision depend on 'regulations issued by him.' That assumes and relies on his power to make rules, and under the definition and Example 6, rulemaking authority counts as participation. The tempting 'No' treats the section as only rewriting definitions. It misses this rulemaking clause, which brings in the public through the rulemaking process.
opus.s: unless the Housing Expediter issues an order decontrolling them, which he shall issue if he finds that the conversion resulted in additional, self  contained family units as defined by regulations issued by him
opus.b: The tempting reading is "No," because most of this section just redefines exempt housing (hotels, trailers, new construction) and the term "rent." But one clause refers to the Housing Expediter's regulatory authority. The definition and Example 6 count authority to issue regulations as participation, because rulemaking brings in public comment.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Housing and Rent Act by providing specific definitions for 'hotel' and 'transient occupancy' to determine which housing accommodations are subject to rent control. It does not establish any process for public consultation, comment periods, advisory committees with non-federal members, or coordination with outside entities before a federal decision is made. The text is purely definitional and regulatory, setting criteria for the application of the law rather than inviting participation in the decision-making process.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the definition of "hotel" or "transient occupancy" involves the general public (tenants), and thus implies participation. However, these are merely statutory definitions used to determine the scope of rent control regulations. They do not establish a process for the public to consult with the government, comment on rules, or participate in decision-making. The text is purely definitional and regulatory in nature, setting criteria for what constitutes controlled housing. There is no mechanism for outside parties to influence the decision-making process described here.
